validated_results.title: Serum micronutrients and prostate cancer in Japanese Americans in Hawaii.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study within a Japanese-American cohort reporting an odds ratio for incident prostate cancer by serum beta-carotene quartile.

extraction.comparison_type: highest versus lowest quartile of serum beta-carotene
extraction.timing: prospective (blood collected 1971-1975 with >20 years of surveillance)

sample_size.excerpt: After a surveillance period of more than 20 years, 142 tissue-confirmed incident cases of prostate cancer were identified. Their stored sera and those of 142 matched controls were measured by high-performance liquid chromatography for the following: total carotenoids, lutein, zeaxanthin, beta-cryptoxanthin, lycopene, alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, total retinoids, retinol, total tocopherols, alpha-tocopherol, delta-tocopherol, and gamma-tocopherol.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 142 + 142 = 284

cases.excerpt: After a surveillance period of more than 20 years, 142 tissue-confirmed incident cases of prostate cancer were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: The odds ratio for the highest quartiles were 1.8 (95% confidence interval, 0.9-3.9) for beta-cryptoxanthin, 1.6 (0.8-3.5) for beta-carotene, 0.8 (0.4-1.5) for retinol, and 0.7 (0.3-1.5) for gamma-tocopherol, but none of the differences was statistically significant.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The odds ratio for the highest quartiles were 1.8 (95% confidence interval, 0.9-3.9) for beta-cryptoxanthin, 1.6 (0.8-3.5) for beta-carotene, 0.8 (0.4-1.5) for retinol, and 0.7 (0.3-1.5) for gamma-tocopherol, but none of the differences was statistically significant.
